merger_description:
Danone S.A. (together with its subsidiaries, **Danone**) proposes to acquire 100% of the issued share capital in Tucker Holdco Pty Ltd (together with its subsidiaries, **MADE**).

Danone is a global food-products corporation, headquartered in France. Globally, Danone supplies dairy products, plant-based foods, bottled plain water and specialised nutrition solutions. In Australia, Danone supplies dairy-based yoghurt under brands such as Activia, Liddells, Ultimate and YoPro. Danone also supplies specialised nutrition solutions under its Nutricia brand (including AptaGrow, Aptamil, Fortijuice, Fortini, Fortisip, Karicare, Loprofin, Souvenaide) and bottled plain water under its Evian brand.

MADE is an Australian food and beverages company headquartered in Melbourne, Australia. MADE supplies dairy-based products under the Rokeby brand, coconut-based beverages and yoghurt under the Cocobella and Nakula brands, pressed juices under the Impressed Juices brand, and flavoured multi-vitamin bottled water under the NutrientWater brand.

In parallel with Danone’s acquisition of MADE, MADE proposes to acquire the remaining 50% of shares that it does not already own in Made (MJV) Pte. Ltd. (**Made JV**). Made JV is a joint venture entity that is part of MADE’s Thailand-based manufacturing operation and held pursuant to a joint venture with Magna Access Co. Ltd, an entity associated with Thailand-based food products manufacturer Chabaa Group. Made JV's operating subsidiary, Made Manufacturing (Thailand) Ltd, manufactures coconut-based products sold by MADE.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and publicly available information.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
▪ The market share aggregation resulting from the Acquisition is
estimated to be low in the supply of dairy and non-dairy yoghurt.
▪ Post-Acquisition, the merged entity would continue to face
competition from alternative suppliers of dairy and non-dairy
yoghurt in Australia, including Bega, Chobani, Coyo, Lactalis, Raw
C and Vitasoy.
